- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3), model underestimates upward momentum — add 2–4% to forecast mean for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon — shift forecast baseline up by 0.5–1.5% relative to 18d average.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak (e.g., -0.4 → +0.2), model delays reaction — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs — if 3 consecutive days show +2%+ and sentiment is flat, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
